19027-the-revolt-on-venus.title: The Revolt On Venus
19027-the-revolt-on-venus.creator: Carey Rockwell
19027-the-revolt-on-venus.description: A book by Carey Rockwell. Seated in front of the scanner screen on the control deck of the rocket cruiser _Polaris_, Captain Steve Strong replaced the microphone in its slot and watched a bulky figure in a space suit step out of the air lock and drift away from the side of the ship.

59983-the-conceited-pig.title: The Conceited Pig
59983-the-conceited-pig.creator: Unknown
59983-the-conceited-pig.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The little pig did not dare answer his mother, so he lay quite still for a minute or two, hoping that he should hear the same noise again. And presently he did hear it, louder than before, and there could be no doubt that more than usual was going on about the premises. He looked round to see what his mother would say now; but she had fallen fast asleep again, and two or three of his brothers were snoring very loud.

arxiv-2112-06031.title: Unsupervised Image to Image translation for multiple retinal pathology synthesis in optical coherence tomography scans
arxiv-2112-06031.creator: Hemanth Pasupuleti, G. N. Girish
arxiv-2112-06031.description: Abstract Image to Image Translation (I2I) is a challenging computer vision problem used in numerous domains for multiple tasks. Recently, ophthalmology became one of the major fields where the application of I2I is increasing rapidly. One such application is the generation of synthetic retinal optical coherence tomographic (OCT) scans.

arxiv-2206-03814.title: Some remarks on non-singular spherically symmetric space-times
arxiv-2206-03814.creator: Lorenzo Sebastiani, Sergio Zerbini
arxiv-2206-03814.description: Abstract A short review on spherically symmetric static regular black holes and spherically symmetric non singular cosmological space-time is presented. Several models of regular black holes, including new ones, are considered. First, a large class of regular black holes having an inner de Sitter core with the related issue of Cauchy horizon is investigated.

arxiv-2301-00026.title: Killing Horizons Decohere Quantum Superpositions
arxiv-2301-00026.creator: Daine L. Danielson, Gautam Satishchandran, Robert M. Wald
arxiv-2301-00026.description: Abstract We recently showed that if a massive (or charged) body is put in a quantum spatial superposition, the mere presence of a black hole in its vicinity will eventually decohere the superposition. In this paper we show that, more generally, decoherence of stationary superpositions will occur in any spacetime with a Killing horizon.

arxiv-2303-06848.title: Advantage of Hardy’s Nonlocal Correlation in Reverse Zero-Error Channel Coding
arxiv-2303-06848.creator: Mir Alimuddin, Ananya Chakraborty, Govind Lal Sidhardh, Ram Krishna Patra, Samrat Sen, Snehasish Roy Chowdhury, Sahil Gopalkrishna Naik, Manik Banik
arxiv-2303-06848.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mir Alimuddin, Ananya Chakraborty, Govind Lal Sidhardh, Ram Krishna Patra, Samrat Sen, Snehasish Roy Chowdhury, Sahil Gopalkrishna Naik, Manik Banik. Hardy’s argument constitutes an elegant proof of quantum nonlocality. In this work, we report an exotic application of Hardy’s nonlocal correlations in two-party communication setup.

arxiv-2404-15783.title: Feature Selection Techniques for CR Isotope Identification with the AMS-02 Experiment in Space
arxiv-2404-15783.creator: Marta Borchiellini * \orcidicon, Leandro Mano \orcidicon, Fernando Barão \orcidicon, Manuela Vecchi \orcidicon
arxiv-2404-15783.description: Abstract Isotopic composition measurements of singly charged cosmic rays (CR) provide essential insights into CR transport in the Galaxy. The Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS-02) can identify singly charged isotopes up to about 10 GeV/n. However, their identification presents challenges due to the small abundance of CR deuterons compared to the proton background.

pmc-10772929.title: Severe Aortic Regurgitation From Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm Prolapse
pmc-10772929.creator: Rachel A. Moshman, Daniel A. Ricketti, Joanne K. Mazzarelli
pmc-10772929.description: Graphical abstract Introduction Sinus of Valsalva aneurysm (SVA) results from weakness of the elastic lamina at the junction of the aortic media and annulus fibrosus. Sinus of Valsalva aneurysm is usually asymptomatic until rupture. We present a case of an unruptured SVA causing severe aortic regurgitation and decompensated heart failure.

pmc-10801100.title: Decolonial health literature can increase our thinking about ethics dumping
pmc-10801100.creator: Cornelius Ewuoso
pmc-10801100.description: This article draws on the underexplored or novel accounts of inclusion and the moral accounts of decolonization in African health decolonial literature to increase our understanding of how ethics dumping manifests in health research partnerships, and what more ought to be done to eliminate this phenomenon.

pmc-11381816.title: Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibition in Patients With Myocardial Injury Complicating Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
pmc-11381816.creator: Daijiro Tomii, Dik Heg, Jonas Lanz, Masaaki Nakase, Daryoush Samim, Stefan Stortecky, David Reineke, Stephan Windecker, Thomas Pilgrim
pmc-11381816.description: BackgroundPeriprocedural myocardial injury impacts clinical outcome after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The optimal medical management strategy for TAVR-related periprocedural myocardial injury has not been established.ObjectivesThe authors aimed to investigate the prognostic association of renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors in patients with periprocedural myocardial injury after TAVR.

pmc-11518526.title: 4.N. Scientific session: Equity in Child Health: Leveraging Universal Health Promotion Services for Families Amid Uncertainty
pmc-11518526.creator: Organised by: Norwegian Institute of Public Health (Norway), Chair persons: Boye Welde (Norway)
pmc-11518526.description: This workshop addresses the urgent need to foster resilience and equity in child health within the context of an increasingly uncertain Europe. Rapid societal changes, exacerbated by events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and heightened risks of conflict, climate change and economic instability, underscore the importance of nurturing environments where children can thrive despite challenging circumstances.

pmc-11639863.title: High Mobility Group Box 1 (HMGB1): Molecular Signaling and Potential Therapeutic Strategies
pmc-11639863.creator: Sayantap Datta, Mohammad Atiqur Rahman, Saisudha Koka, Krishna M. Boini
pmc-11639863.description: High Mobility Group Box 1 (HMGB1) is a highly conserved non-histone chromatin-associated protein across species, primarily recognized for its regulatory impact on vital cellular processes, like autophagy, cell survival, and apoptosis. HMGB1 exhibits dual functionality based on its localization: both as a non-histone protein in the nucleus and as an inducer of inflammatory cytokines upon extracellular release.

pmc-12800365.title: RNA-seq-derived sequence variations are excellent features for cell line identification
pmc-12800365.creator: Lisa Müller, Simon Müller, Khursheed Ul Islam Mir, Jana Lange, Sven Hagemann, Alice Wedler, Frank Hause, Claudia Misiak, Danny Misiak, Tony Gutschner, Stefan Hüttelmaier, Markus Glaß
pmc-12800365.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Cell lines are indispensable models for analyzing molecular mechanisms underlying human diseases. However, incorrect annotation and cross-contamination can introduce severe bias in respective studies. Accordingly, various publishers request authentication of cell lines before publication. Short tandem repeat profiling is commonly used to verify cell line identity and purity but does not guarantee that published results are based on the samples tested by this method. In this study, we demonstrate that RNA-seq-derived sequence variation information is eligible for unambiguous cell line-specific clustering.

pmc-13049428.title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis from a multiscale mechanobiology perspective: Mechanisms and future therapeutic prospects
pmc-13049428.creator: Tingting Xia, Xi Wang, Zhao Yang, Runze Zhao
pmc-13049428.description: SummaryIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a fatal interstitial lung disease that induces irreversible fibrosis and architectural remodeling. Traditional inflammation-based theories fall short in explaining its pathological processes, regional heterogeneity, and spatially biased lesion distribution. Recent studies have highlighted the critical role of biomechanical microenvironment, ranging from the molecular and cellular level to the whole-organ scale, in driving fibrotic progression.

pmc-13211867.title: Perspectives and Needs Regarding Remote Monitoring Technologies Among South Asian Individuals Living With Long-Term Conditions in the United Kingdom: Semistructured Interview and Focus Group Study
pmc-13211867.creator: Syed Mustafa Ali, Yumna Masood, Karen Staniland, William G Dixon, Sabine N van der Veer, Caroline Sanders
pmc-13211867.description: BackgroundSouth Asian individuals face a higher burden of long-term conditions while also experiencing more inequities in health care access and outcomes. Despite the potential of remote monitoring technologies to improve management of long-term conditions, South Asian individuals are less likely to engage with digital health interventions and are underrepresented in health research, partly due to language barriers.

pmc-13245448.title: Association of TyG with Survival and Metabolic Alterations in Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome: A Single- Centre Retrospective Study
pmc-13245448.creator: Long Zeng, Fengqin Zhou, Ling Wu, Ailin Wang, Huai Liu, Guojun Du, Chunxia Guo, Tao Zhang
pmc-13245448.description: PurposeThis single-center retrospective study aimed to assess the correlation between triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) and prognosis in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) and investigate its correlation with metabolic alterations.MethodsA total of 754 patients diagnosed with SFTS at Wuhan Union Hospital between January 2022 and April 2024 were enrolled.

pmc-13316890.creator: Carmen Trumello, Angela Ferrucci, Lucia Lombardi, Milena Mancini, Ilaria Basadonne, Silvio Mignogna, Camilla Milano, Tânia Brandão, Alessandra Babore
pmc-13316890.description: Objectivethis study, grounded in attachment theory and situated within the debate between categorical and dimensional approaches to attachment, aims to pursue two complementary objectives: firstly, to examine the differences in physical and mental health across different attachment styles; secondly, to analyze the specific contribution of internal working models (IWMs) in explaining these variations, allowing for an integrated interpretation of the

pmc-13386806.title: Comparison of the efficacy of different types and intensities of extracorporeal shock wave therapy for lateral epicondylitis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-13386806.creator: Ran Jin, Haijing Wang, Wenwen Lv, Hengqiang Cheng, Yanru Li, Qingqiang Yuan
pmc-13386806.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTo evaluate the efficacy of different types and intensities of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) for lateral epicondylitis using a network meta-analysis.MethodsFollowing a systematic retrieval of major databases (e.g. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library) from their respective inception dates up to September 2025, relevant RCTs and cohort studies on ESWT for lateral epicondylitis were identified, with data analyzed in R software (version 4.4.3).ResultsThe analysis included 11 RCTs and 2 cohort studies involving 938 patients with lateral epicondylitis.

pmc-13488553.title: Psychological outcomes following digital replantation and revascularization: A narrative review
pmc-13488553.creator: Diana Mastellone, Dev Patel, Kenyon Graham, Michael J. Franco
pmc-13488553.description: PurposeLiterature on digital replantation has historically prioritized primary outcomes such as viability rates, return-to-work timelines, and restoration of range of motion and grip strength. Psychological and psychosocial sequelae, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, anxiety, sleep disturbance, adjustment disorder, and body image disruption, are reported inconsistently, infrequently, or not at all.

pmc-13633395.title: Treatment and Return to Sport in Athletes With Scaphoid Fractures: A Narrative Review
pmc-13633395.creator: Yolanda Gutierrez, Paul Bonilla, Emmanuel Franco, Ronald Shaju, Alyssa Sepulveda, Nicholas Bonazza, Robert Schenck, Aamir Ahmad
pmc-13633395.description: Scaphoid fractures are the most common fracture of the carpal bone and frequently occur in athletic populations due to acute trauma or repetitive wrist loading. Management of these injuries in athletes is challenging because of the need to balance reliable fracture healing with timely return to sport.
